messages:
Nina (Support): @here customer sent a screen recording (Android app behind corp proxy) but no visible req id. Need a short playbook: how to get a req/trace id from a screen recording + the minimal curl we should ask for to repro. :wave:

Raj (Support Lead): Short checklist: 1) ask customer for approximate timestamp(s) in the video, 2) ask for a HAR or system logs if they can, 3) ask for an SDK log snippet or adb logcat if Android, 4) provide a copy/paste curl for them to run if possible. Keep it minimal.

Sam (Eng Oncall): For Android behind a proxy the fastest wins: adb logcat (if they can run it) or look for the request header in device logs. Share this one-liner with them: 
```
adb logcat -v time | grep -i "req\|x-req\|request-id" --color=never
```
If you need a stricter extractor (server-side proxies often inject x-req-ref):
```
adb logcat -d | grep -ioE 'x-req-?ref:\s*[0-9a-f]+' | sed -E 's/.*:\s*//'
```
That prints candidate ids.

Sam (Eng Oncall): If you only have the screen recording, ask the customer for the video timestamp (e.g. 00:03:12) where the error happened, then ask for a full-screen screenshot at that frame. Look for any server error UI that prints an error token or tiny alphanumeric id. Also check network indicator bars — if they used a debug overlay it may show request hashes.

Maya (Support): If they can do a HAR from a webview / embedded browser, send these HAR instructions (minimal):
```
1) Open Chrome on desktop (if repro on webview, replicate on desktop).
2) DevTools -> Network -> check "Preserve log" -> reproduce.
3) Right click -> Save all as HAR with content, attach file.
```
If it's mobile-only and they can't run HAR, ask for: system logs + the exact app timestamp + a short screencap clip around the event.

Maya (Support): Minimal message to paste to customer (copy/paste):
```
Hi — thanks for the video. Can you please: 1) tell us the exact timestamp in the video when the error happens (e.g. 00:03:12), 2) attach a screenshot at that frame, 3) if possible run this adb command and paste the output: 

adb logcat -d | grep -i "x-req\|reqref\|request-id" | tail -n 20

4) Or, if you can run a curl to reproduce, please run: 

curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"short text trigger"}'

And paste the full request/response headers (redact sensitive tokens).

Thank you!
```

Raj (Support Lead): Also ask them to look for any UI error token (short hex string) and include network timings. If they can't run adb/har, a high-quality frame (screenshot) + timecode is often enough for us to correlate in proxy logs.

Nina (Support): If we get a screenshot/timecode only, who will own matching in proxy logs? I can try first-pass correlation, ping @Sam if I don't find it in 10 minutes.

Sam (Eng Oncall): I can run a quick grep on the edge logs. Useful server grep patterns: 
```
grep -i "9a[0-9a-f]\{6,}\|x-req-ref" /var/log/edge/*.log | grep "2026-03-17T15:12" -B2 -A2
```
Replace the iso time with the customer-provided timestamp (UTC). If you only have epoch, convert and search the 30s window.

Maya (Support): If customer returns a HAR, we want: request headers (showing x-req-ref / request-id); response status and any body trace token; and timings. Tell them to attach the HAR file rather than screenshots of DevTools.

Nina (Support): Good. I'll message customer with the template. Will post back when they reply.

support-bot: Saved runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/support/screen-to-reqid (useful if you need step-by-step correlation scripts).
